Same word, different measure: comparing source definitions

Report an error

01What does this evidence establish?

The comparison table sets the selected records side by side on definition, population or calculation base, period, method, source and currentness. Check geography and unit in each evidence record before comparing values. Terms such as accounts, active accounts, subscribers, beneficiaries, merchants and POS terminals may sound related but are not interchangeable. Material mismatches remain visible and prevent a false common scale or combined result.

02What does it measure?

This record sets out a comparison rule: records are compared on definition, period, population or calculation base, source scope and method before their values are placed on one scale; it reports no value of its own.

03Who or what does it apply to?

The measures matched in the documented comparison table and the evidence records being compared

04How current is it?

This record sets out a comparison rule and has no observation date of its own; each record compared keeps its own period.

05What this evidence does not establish

The same word does not mean the same measure. The comparison does not reconcile differing figures or prefer one number unless evidence on their definitions supports it.

06Original source and verification

This view summarises other evidence records, which are not yet linked individually here. Before reusing a figure, open the evidence record that reports it and check that record against its own source.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

The recorded fields of each selected record are compared field by field; a difference in any material field marks the pair as not directly comparable, and no value is chosen as the correct one.

When does this record change?

This record is updated when an authoritative source is revised or replaced, a newer comparable observation becomes available, the definition, population or method changes, or the conditions for public use change.

How should this record be read?

Read this evidence within the definition, population or group covered, calculation base where relevant, period, geography and method shown on the page. Before reusing or comparing it, check the source, limitations, evidence date and correction history. If a value or source link is unavailable, the page says so rather than filling the gap by inference. This resource does not host source files; where an original-source link is given, check the publisher’s terms before republishing.
